items.current:
- BROKER qualifies EFFECT_GATE as a peer (artifact, label, cgroup, pidfd/start,
  SO_PEERCRED) before BIND_EXECUTION. EFFECT_GATE qualifies the broker the same way
  on every I05 frame and the writer on every I07 frame.
items.proposed:
- BROKER qualifies EFFECT_GATE as a peer (artifact, label, cgroup, pidfd/start, SO_PEERCRED) before BIND_EXECUTION.
  Its artifact check reads the gate's `/proc/<pid>/exe` link, which the kernel allows as long as the gate holds no
  capability (the signed I04 port is 1024 or above, Q-HE2S-9 (a)), stays dumpable (Q-HE2S-7 (a)) and runs with uids
  and gids 0 that equal the broker's filesystem uid and gid (O-W03-PEER-EXE).
- A peer's start time is compared on every frame with a reference taken without a race at its first frame: the
  qualifier holds a pidfd that names the connected process itself (SO_PEERPIDFD, or SCM_PIDFD on a frame), reads
  `/proc/<pid>/stat`, and then confirms through that pidfd (poll) that the process has not exited, so the entry was
  that process's. A pidfd_open of the SO_PEERCRED pid alone does not give such a reference, because that pid may
  already name a later process (HS43).
- EFFECT_GATE qualifies the broker on every I05 frame by label, cgroup, pidfd/start and SO_PEERCRED (HS43). It does
  not check the broker's artifact. Reading `/proc/<pid>/exe` is a ptrace-mode read (PTRACE_MODE_READ_FSCREDS);
  without CAP_SYS_PTRACE, which no role holds, the kernel allows it only if the target's permitted capabilities are a
  subset of the reader's effective ones, and the broker's (§5.3) are not a subset of the gate's, so the kernel
  refuses the gate that read. The broker's executable identity follows from its label instead: SELinux matrix v4
  (`architecture/selinux-matrix-v2/`) lets `planeon_broker_t` be entered only from init through
  `planeon_broker_exec_t` and denies `execute_no_trans` on every type, so the label identifies the executable as long
  as only the enrolled broker artifact carries that type.
- EFFECT_GATE qualifies the writer on every I07 frame by artifact, label, cgroup, pidfd/start and SO_PEERCRED (HS43).
  For the artifact it opens the `/proc/<pid>` directory of the pidfd's process and confirms through the pidfd that
  the process is still alive after the open, so no PID reuse can intervene, then reads its `exe` link with
  `readlinkat` on that directory descriptor (§5.3) into a buffer longer than the enrolled writer path (§4.2); the
  link must equal that path exactly, with no " (deleted)" suffix. The fs-verity digest is enforced on the sealed file
  the path names (§4.2, at enrollment); the gate does not re-measure it per frame, which would need
  FS_IOC_MEASURE_VERITY, an ioctl its allowlist does not admit. The kernel allows the read without CAP_SYS_PTRACE
  only while the gate's filesystem uid and gid equal the writer's real, effective and saved uids and gids (all 0),
  the writer is dumpable, and the writer's permitted capabilities are a subset of the gate's effective ones, which
  the writer's empty set (§5.3) always is; SELinux matrix v4 gives `planeon_gate_t` `file read` on
  `planeon_policy_writer_t` (`procAccess`), the LSM check of that read. Yama (ptrace_scope 3) limits only ptrace
  attach, not this read, and /proc must be mounted with hidepid=0 (the default), or the gate loses sight of its
  peers' entries. Obligation O-W03-WRITER-EXE holds both sides to this. Until the gate's filter admits `readlinkat`
  (O-SECCOMP-V3-READLINKAT), the writer's artifact check is decided but open (Q-HE3A-1b) and the other four checks
  apply.
items.why: The gate cannot read the broker's exe link (commoncap: the target's permitted set must lie in the reader's effective set), so the broker is qualified without an artifact check and identified by its label (Q-HE2S-10, Q-HS43-1); the writer keeps the artifact check through its exe link (Q-HE3A-1 (c)) under the kernel's stated preconditions; the broker's check of the gate holds because the gate has no capability (Q-HE2S-9) and stays dumpable (Q-HE2S-7); the start time is compared with a race-free reference, so pidfd/start closes the PID-reuse window (Q-HS43-1).

Stated residuals:

- R-WRITER-PROC: A dumpable writer lets every uid-0 role with procAccess on it read its ptrace-gated entries, for example exe, cwd, root, fd, fdinfo, environ and maps: the server, the observer and the broker as well as the gate. mem and process_vm_* stay refused, because they need ptrace attach, which Yama ptrace_scope 3 refuses. Follow-up: obligation O-MATRIX-WRITER-PROCACCESS, in the queued SELinux matrix amendment SELINUX-MATRIX-I04-KEYCERT (Q-HS43-3).
- R-GATE-PROC: The gate stays dumpable (Q-HE2S-7 (a)) and holds no capability, so every uid-0 role with procAccess on it (the broker, the server and the observer) can read its ptrace-gated entries, for example environ, maps, cwd and the fd links; reopening a credential through an fd link still meets SELinux's file checks on the credential type (matrix v4 A09). mem and process_vm_* stay refused, because they need ptrace attach, which Yama ptrace_scope 3 refuses. Follow-up: obligation O-MATRIX-GATE-PROCACCESS, in the queued SELinux matrix amendment SELINUX-MATRIX-I04-KEYCERT (Q-HS43-3, Q-HE2S-7).

The data follow in order (Q-HE3A-1b): the W02d v3 allowlist (`architecture/seccomp-allowlists-v3/`) gains the
EFFECT_GATE `readlinkat` rule in its own packet, then the EFFECT_GATE programs and the edge record are republished,
then R10 re-vendors them and adds the check.

Obligations: O-SECCOMP-V3-READLINKAT (the allowlist rule), O-W03-WRITER-EXE (the writer's credentials and dumpability, and the read bound to the frame's process), O-W03-PEER-EXE (the gate readable by the broker, and race-free peer pidfds), O-MATRIX-WRITER-PROCACCESS (narrowing the writer's /proc readers, residual R-WRITER-PROC), O-MATRIX-GATE-PROCACCESS (narrowing the gate's /proc readers, residual R-GATE-PROC), O-T04-HS43 (native confirmation). Every E01-E12 obligation stays OPEN_UNPROVEN.

dispositions.summary: The gate qualifies the broker by label, cgroup, pidfd/start and SO_PEERCRED; its executable identity follows from its label; the BIND digest is the mutual record with the narrower gate-side half.
The gate stays dumpable, so the broker can read its exe link; its other gated entries are residual R-GATE-PROC.
The gate holds no capability (H5), so its permitted set lies inside the broker's.
The gate checks the writer's executable through its exe link, under the kernel's ptrace-read rules.
The specification states the readlinkat duty; the allowlist rule follows in its own packet.
The duty admits readlinkat only with a dirfd other than AT_FDCWD (a non-negative int).
Only the artifact is dropped; pidfd/start stays, compared with a race-free reference.
The closed list of adopted clauses HS43 overrides (I05 v1-v3, I07 v1 as inherited by v2 and v3, W01 §7, the matrix v4 README) is quoted exactly under supersedes; their files stay byte-identical.
The dumpable writer's and gate's gated /proc entries are stated residuals; the queued matrix amendment must evaluate narrowing who reads them.
The duty's dirfd rule is a non-negative int, one masked condition in the next packet.

obligations.label: the allowlist rule
obligations.owner: the parallel lane's next harness-onion packet (the W02d v3 allowlist amendment, Q-HE3A-1b)
obligations.text: Add to the EFFECT_GATE row of architecture/seccomp-allowlists-v3/ a readlinkat rule for x86_64 and aarch64 that admits only a non-negative dirfd judged on the low 32 bits of argument 0, which refuses AT_FDCWD (0xffffff9c) whatever the upper bits and any other negative value; one masked condition, (arg0 & 0x80000000) == 0, expresses it in the v3 model. Keep readlink unlisted, change no other role, and republish the vectors with AT_FDCWD in both encodings (0xffffffffffffff9c and 0x00000000ffffff9c) and -1 as killed cases.

obligations.label: the writer's credentials and dumpability, and the read bound to the frame's process
obligations.owner: W03 (the writer and the gate's I07 check; HE-007 per owner decision Q-HE3A-1b)
obligations.text: Run the writer with real, effective and saved uid and gid 0 and an empty permitted capability set, and keep it dumpable: no PR_SET_DUMPABLE 0, and an exec that changes no credentials (an artifact with no set-id bit and no file capabilities, started with equal uids and gids, and readable by the starting domain, planeon_admin_t, which matrix v4 gives READ on planeon_policy_writer_exec_t). Empty its capabilities without letting the exec raise any (for example SECBIT_NOROOT and an empty bounding set in the starter), so the exec's capability recomputation neither grants capabilities nor clears dumpability. Run the gate with filesystem uid and gid 0. Take the writer's pidfd from the socket (SO_PEERPIDFD or SCM_PIDFD), open /proc/<pid> for that process with no PID-reuse window, read the exe link into a buffer longer than the enrolled path, and accept it only if it equals that path exactly.

obligations.label: the gate readable by the broker, and race-free peer pidfds
obligations.text: Keep the gate dumpable (Q-HE2S-7 (a)), with uid and gid 0 and no capability after its seal (Q-HE2S-9 (a)), so the broker's read of its exe link passes the kernel's ptrace-read rules; take every peer pidfd from the socket (SO_PEERPIDFD at accept or SCM_PIDFD on a frame) or otherwise race-free, so a pidfd_open of a SO_PEERCRED pid is never the only reference; read each peer's start time once from /proc/<pid>/stat and then confirm through that pidfd that the process has not exited. Run the broker with filesystem uid and gid 0, equal to the gate's uids and gids.

obligations.label: narrowing the writer's /proc readers, residual R-WRITER-PROC
obligations.owner: the queued SELinux matrix amendment SELINUX-MATRIX-I04-KEYCERT (parallel lane, after SECCOMP-V3-READLINKAT)
obligations.text: Evaluate narrowing planeon_policy_writer_t's procAccess to planeon_gate_t alone, so the dumpable writer's ptrace-gated entries (exe, cwd, root, fd, fdinfo, environ, maps) are no longer readable by the server, the observer and the broker; record the outcome and its reason in that amendment (owner decision Q-HS43-3 (a)).

obligations.label: narrowing the gate's /proc readers, residual R-GATE-PROC
obligations.owner: the queued SELinux matrix amendment SELINUX-MATRIX-I04-KEYCERT (parallel lane, after SECCOMP-V3-READLINKAT)
obligations.text: Evaluate which of the server's and the observer's reads of planeon_gate_t's ptrace-gated /proc entries their captures need, and narrow the rest; the broker keeps the gate's exe link for its artifact check. Record the outcome and its reason in that amendment (owner decision Q-HS43-3 (a), applied to the gate, which Q-HE2S-7 (a) keeps dumpable).

obligations.label: native confirmation
obligations.text: On the enrolled kernel, confirm: the gate's readlinkat of the writer's exe link succeeds under the gate's filter and the writer's credentials; the same read of the broker's exe link fails with EACCES (an audited `capability sys_ptrace` denial for planeon_gate_t is expected, not a breach); the broker can read the gate's exe link; on x86_64 readlink kills the gate, and on both architectures readlinkat with AT_FDCWD in either encoding, or with -1, kills it; and the exact-path comparison refuses a longer path and a " (deleted)" target.

residuals.text: A dumpable writer lets every uid-0 role with procAccess on it read its ptrace-gated entries, for example exe, cwd, root, fd, fdinfo, environ and maps: the server, the observer and the broker as well as the gate. mem and process_vm_* stay refused, because they need ptrace attach, which Yama ptrace_scope 3 refuses.
residuals.followUp: obligation O-MATRIX-WRITER-PROCACCESS, in the queued SELinux matrix amendment SELINUX-MATRIX-I04-KEYCERT

residuals.text: The gate stays dumpable (Q-HE2S-7 (a)) and holds no capability, so every uid-0 role with procAccess on it (the broker, the server and the observer) can read its ptrace-gated entries, for example environ, maps, cwd and the fd links; reopening a credential through an fd link still meets SELinux's file checks on the credential type (matrix v4 A09). mem and process_vm_* stay refused, because they need ptrace attach, which Yama ptrace_scope 3 refuses.
residuals.followUp: obligation O-MATRIX-GATE-PROCACCESS, in the queued SELinux matrix amendment SELINUX-MATRIX-I04-KEYCERT
